name: Várzea Grande–Marechal Rondon International Airport
before:
The airport for Cuiabá, 10 km from downtown in the neighbouring municipality of Várzea Grande, and the practical arrival for Mato Grosso.

Capacity has been a problem here. An Infraero assessment in 2011 listed Cuiabá as critically saturated, running above 85 per cent of capacity, which is the worst category on that list. A new terminal was built in phases from 2006 and further money went in ahead of the 2014 World Cup, when Cuiabá was a host city, covering the terminal, parking and access roads.

Aeroeste has run the airport under a 30-year concession since March 2019, taking over from Infraero.

It was inaugurated in 1956 but worked in fairly rough conditions until the first proper passenger terminal was finished in 1964, and it only gained international status in 1996.

It is named after Marshal Cândido Rondon, the Brazilian explorer.
after:
The airport for Cuiabá, 10 km from the city centre in the neighbouring municipality of Várzea Grande, and the practical arrival for Mato Grosso.

Centro-Oeste Airports, part of the Socicam group, took over from Infraero in December 2019. The terminal has since been enlarged and modernised, with up to 50 per cent more space.

It is named after Marshal Cândido Rondon, the Brazilian explorer.

Aeroeste was the consortium of Socicam and Sinart that won the Mato Grosso block, Cuiabá included, in 2019 (Agência Brasil, September 2019); the airport is run today under the name Centro-Oeste Airports, which DECEA's live entry gives as operator and Socicam calls a Socicam group company.

claims.claim: took over from Infraero in December 2019

claims.note: Was 'under a 30-year concession since March 2019'. March 2019 was the auction (Wikipedia: won on 15 March 2019); the operator took charge in December 2019 (Socicam, and RD News reporting the operator's figures), and Wikipedia's traffic table switches from Infraero to COA reports in 2020, which fits. The 30-year term rests on Wikipedia alone.

O Marechal Rondon é administrado pela empresa Centro Oeste Airports (COA) desde 2019, quando saiu da gestão da Empresa Brasileira de Infraestrutura Aeroportuária (Infraero).

claims.claim: terminal enlarged and modernised, up to 50 per cent more space
claims.inAfter: The terminal has since been enlarged and modernised, with up to 50 per cent more space.
claims.note: Replaces the old terminal and capacity paragraph (the 2011 saturation list and the 2006 to 2014 terminal works), which the concessionaire's works have overtaken. About R$280 million since December 2019; the departure lounge is about 39 per cent bigger and the hall 21 per cent (both sources). The works were still unfinished in April 2023 (Socicam).

claims.note: The airport is Marechal Rondon to DECEA and its operator; the Brazilian Army's page on Cândido Mariano da Silva Rondon records his rank of marshal (1955) and calls him the explorer who went deepest into tropical lands.

claims.wasBefore: An Infraero assessment in 2011 listed Cuiabá as critically saturated, running above 85 per cent of capacity, which is the worst category on that list.
claims.why: Fifteen years old and overtaken by the 2019 to 2023 enlargement; the figures rest on Wikipedia alone and 'the worst category' was not in any source.

claims.claim: terminal built in phases from 2006; World Cup money for terminal, parking and access
claims.wasBefore: A new terminal was built in phases from 2006 and further money went in ahead of the 2014 World Cup, when Cuiabá was a host city, covering the terminal, parking and access roads.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone (Infraero's own site answered 'Request Rejected'), and overtaken by the concessionaire's enlargement.

claims.wasBefore: Aeroeste has run the airport under a 30-year concession since March 2019, taking over from Infraero.
claims.why: March 2019 was the auction: the Aeroeste consortium (Socicam and Sinart) won the Mato Grosso block (Agência Brasil). Centro-Oeste Airports, the Socicam company named by DECEA and Socicam, took over in December 2019, which the text now says. The 30-year term rests on Wikipedia and Agência Brasil's figure for all three 2019 blocks together, so it is not repeated.

claims.claim: inaugurated 1956, rough conditions until the 1964 terminal
claims.wasBefore: It was inaugurated in 1956 but worked in fairly rough conditions until the first proper passenger terminal was finished in 1964
claims.why: Wikipedia alone; Infraero's site answered 'Request Rejected' and no other history of the airport was found.

claims.wasBefore: and it only gained international status in 1996
claims.why: The 1996 date rests on Wikipedia alone and misleads: RD News says the airport was international in name only, with no regular commercial international flights for 26 years, until an ANAC ordinance of December 2024 cleared it for regular international flights (DECEA and Socicam confirm the clearance, not the date). Not replaced, because 'cleared for international flights' alone would suggest flights that do not yet run; see the report for the owner.

opinion.text: and the practical arrival for Mato Grosso
opinion.why: Judgement kept from the old text: it serves Cuiabá, the state capital (GeoNames), and the concessionaire's own 2025 figures put Sinop, the next busiest, second in Mato Grosso (RD News, January 2026).
